name: The Nyingma preliminaries (sngon 'gro)
method_summary: The complete foundation of the Longchen Nyingthig and other cycles: the outer preliminaries (reflection on the freedoms and advantages, impermanence, the defects of saṃsāra, karma, the benefits of liberation, following a teacher) and the inner preliminaries (refuge with prostrations, bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala, kusāli, guru yoga), traditionally each accumulated a hundred thousand times, followed by the transference of consciousness.
duration: traditionally completed over months or years (five sets of 100,000)

name: The four thoughts that turn the mind (blo ldog rnam bzhi)
method_summary: Repeated contemplation of the precious human birth, impermanence and death, the defects of saṃsāra and cause and effect, until the mind turns from worldly aims; practised at the start of every session.
notes: Also taught in the Kagyu and Sakya preliminaries (other units).

name: Refuge and prostration
method_summary: Visualizing the refuge tree (Padmasambhava and the lineage, yidams, buddhas, dharma, sangha, ḍākinīs and protectors), reciting the refuge prayer and prostrating, with the whole of beings, until enlightenment.

warnings.text: Refuge carries precepts (not taking refuge in worldly gods, not harming beings, respecting images and texts); breaking them weakens the refuge.

name: Generating the awakening mind
method_summary: In the Nyingma preliminaries: training in the four boundless attitudes, taking the vow of aspiring and applying bodhicitta, equalizing and exchanging self and others, and taking on others' suffering.

name: Vajrasattva meditation and recitation (the hundred-syllable mantra)
method_summary: Vajrasattva is visualized above the head; with the four powers (support, regret, resolution, antidote) one recites the hundred-syllable mantra while nectar flows down, washing out wrongdoing and obscurations; Vajrasattva declares them purified and dissolves into oneself.
signs_of_progress: dreams of bathing, vomiting impurities, wearing white, flying (purification signs)

name: Maṇḍala offering
method_summary: Arranging heaps on a maṇḍala plate as Mount Meru, the continents and all treasures, and offering the universe, one's body, wealth and merit to the refuge — to perfect the accumulations of merit and wisdom.

name: The kusāli's accumulation (offering the body)
method_summary: The renunciant's offering: visualizing one's consciousness as a wrathful ḍākinī who cuts off the body's skull as a cauldron, transforms the body into nectar and offers it to the buddhas and to all guests, cutting attachment to the body. A visualization only; related to Chöd (owned by U48).

name: Guru yoga (bla ma'i rnal 'byor)
method_summary: Visualizing one's teacher as Padmasambhava (or in Bön as Tapihritsa or Shenrab), making the seven-branch offering, supplicating with the Seven-line prayer and Vajra Guru mantra, receiving the four empowerments by lights from the guru's three places, and mingling one's mind with the guru's wisdom mind, then resting in that state; the root of blessing and realization in Dzogchen.

name: Recitation of the Seven-line prayer
method_summary: Recitation of the seven-line invocation of Padmasambhava, alone or at the start of guru yoga and other practices.

name: The Vajra Guru mantra
method_summary: Recitation of oṃ āḥ hūṃ vajra guru padma siddhi hūṃ, the mantra of Padmasambhava, in guru yoga and as a continuous devotional practice.

name: Mahāyoga generation stage (bskyed rim)
method_summary: From the three samādhis (suchness, all-illuminating compassion, the seed syllable) the practitioner generates the maṇḍala and deity, with clear appearance, vajra pride and recollection of purity, purifying the habits of birth, and recites the mantra; everything is seen as deity, sound as mantra, thought as wisdom.

name: Approach and accomplishment (bsnyen sgrub)
method_summary: The fourfold structure of deity practice — approach, close approach, accomplishment, great accomplishment — with mantra counts fixed by the sādhana, often in retreat.

name: Practice of the Eight Herukas (bka' brgyad)
method_summary: Sādhanas of the eight heruka classes, singly or gathered in one maṇḍala (as in Nyangral's Kagye Deshek Düpa).

name: Vajrakīla practice
method_summary: Sādhana of the wrathful Vajrakīla, embodiment of enlightened activity, to remove obstacles, practised in major Nyingma cycles and in annual monastic ceremonies.

name: The 'liberation' rite (sgrol ba)
method_summary: A wrathful tantric rite in which the consciousness of a being causing great harm is, by tradition, liberated into a pure realm, performed on an effigy (liṅga). Recorded as a summary only.

warnings.text: Tradition allows it only to one who can actually transfer the consciousness to a pure realm and acts out of compassion; performed otherwise it is a grave downfall that harms the performer.

name: Feast offering (tshogs 'khor, gaṇacakra)
method_summary: A gathering in which food and drink are consecrated as nectar and offered to the deities and guests, with confession and restoration of samaya; held on the tenth and twenty-fifth days of the lunar month.

name: Great accomplishment and sacred-medicine accomplishment
method_summary: Collective, uninterrupted sādhana over several days, often producing consecrated medicine pills.

name: Torma offering
method_summary: Offering sculpted ritual cakes to deities, protectors and spirits, or using them as supports of the deity.

name: Smoke offering (bsang)
method_summary: Burning juniper and substances with prayers to purify and to please the deities, protectors and local spirits.

name: Long-life practice (tshe sgrub)
method_summary: Sādhana of long-life deities (Amitāyus, Padmasambhava as Tsepakme with Mandāravā) to extend life and restore vitality.

name: Anuyoga completion stage (rdzogs rim)
method_summary: Work with the channels, winds and essences to bring the winds into the central channel and give rise to bliss-emptiness, emphasized in Anuyoga. Summary only.

warnings.text: Taught only after empowerment and under guidance; improper practice disturbs the winds.

name: Channels and winds (rtsa rlung)
method_summary: Yogic exercises of the channels and winds (visualization of the channels, breath and movement) that prepare for the completion stage and Dzogchen; in Bön from the Mother Tantra and the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü. Summary only.

warnings.text: Forcing the breath or visualization causes wind disorders (srog rlung): practise only as taught and gently.

name: Vase breathing (bum pa can)
method_summary: A gentle retention in which the breath is drawn down and held below the navel in the shape of a vase, used in tsa-lung, inner heat and as the basis of other yogas. Summary only: no counts or durations.

warnings.text: Held forcefully or too long it disturbs the winds and heart; the traditions insist on gentle practice under a teacher's guidance.

notes: Owned by U45 (brief). Also a Kagyu and Gelug practice (other units).

name: The nine-round purification breath (rlung ro dgu bsal)
method_summary: Expelling stale air in three sets of three exhalations — through one nostril, the other and both — while visualizing the three poisons (desire, anger, ignorance) leaving through the side channels and central channel; done at the start of sessions to calm the mind.
notes: Owned by U45 (brief). Which nostril and colour correspond to which poison differs between Nyingma, Bön and Kagyu instructions and between men and women; not specified here.

name: Magical movement ('phrul 'khor)
method_summary: Sequences of movements combined with breath holding, practised in retreat with the completion stage and in Dzogchen (in Bön the trulkhor of the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü). Summary only.

warnings.text: Taught only orally in retreat settings; not to be learned from books.

name: Direct introduction to awareness (ngo sprod)
method_summary: The master points out awareness directly — by word, gesture, symbol or a sudden 'phaṭ' — and the disciple recognizes the nature of mind; the first of Garab Dorje's three statements.

name: Separating saṃsāra and nirvāṇa ('khor 'das ru shan)
method_summary: The extraordinary preliminaries of the Heart-essence: outer (acting out the behaviour of the six realms in solitude and then resting), inner (purifying the seeds of the six realms with syllables) and secret (training body, speech and mind: the vajra posture, the syllable hūṃ, and examining mind's arising, abiding and going), to distinguish ordinary mind from awareness.

warnings.text: To be done in solitude and under guidance; the outer rushen is not for public places.

name: Searching for the mind (sems 'tshol)
method_summary: Examining where mind comes from, where it stays and where it goes, and what its colour and shape are, until its unfindability is seen; part of the secret rushen and of Bön Dzogchen preliminaries.

name: Holding the mind (sems 'dzin)
method_summary: A set of Heart-essence exercises (traditionally twenty-one) using posture, sound, breath and visualization to produce experiences in which awareness can be recognized.

name: Calm abiding in the Great Perfection (zhi gnas)
method_summary: Calm abiding with a support (a letter A, an object, the breath), without support, and natural calm, as a foundation for recognizing awareness; in Bön the fixation on the white A of the A-tri.

name: Cutting through (khregs chod)
method_summary: After direct introduction, resting in fresh, unfabricated awareness, recognizing whatever arises as its display so that it self-liberates, without meditating on an object; view, meditation and conduct are 'left as they are'; the practice of primordial purity.
prerequisites: direct introduction by a qualified master
signs_of_progress: no division between session and post-session

warnings.text: Mistaking a blank, indifferent state (the all-base) or meditative experiences for awareness is the chief deviation.

name: Direct crossing (thod rgal)
method_summary: The instruction-series practice of spontaneous presence: relying on key points of body and gaze given orally by the master, the lamps bring forth the four visions, culminating in the exhaustion of phenomena and possibly the rainbow body. Summary only.
prerequisites: oral instruction from a qualified master

warnings.text: Taught only to those stable in cutting through and only orally by a qualified master; practised without that foundation the visions become mere experiences.
The Heart-essence tantras restrict the instruction to fit vessels; teaching it to the unfit brings harm to both.

name: Dark retreat (mun mtshams)
method_summary: Retreat in complete darkness for a prescribed period, in Nyingma Heart-essence (Yangti) and in the Bön Zhang Zhung Nyengyü, to bring forth the visions of spontaneous presence. Summary only.

warnings.text: Undertaken only with a master's instruction and supervision, after the foundations are complete; the traditions warn of disturbances of wind and mind when it is attempted without them.

notes: RESTRICTED: durations and methods not recorded.

name: Dream yoga (rmi lam)
method_summary: Recognizing dreams as dreams, transforming and mastering them, and training in the bardo of dream as preparation for the bardos after death; with the yoga of luminous sleep. In Bön from the Mother Tantra.
notes: Also one of the Six Yogas of Nāropa (other units).

name: Training for the bardos
method_summary: Practising in life the recognitions to be made after death: resting in the clear light, seeing appearances as self-display, dream yoga, the peaceful and wrathful deities, the root verses of the six bardos.

name: Liberation through hearing (thos grol)
method_summary: Reading the Bardo Thödol aloud to the dying and dead, from the moment of death through the forty-nine days, introducing the clear light and the deities and guiding the consciousness.

name: Transference of consciousness ('pho ba)
method_summary: Training at the moment of death, or in life as preparation, to transfer the consciousness through the crown to a pure land or into the guru's heart; five kinds are distinguished. Summary only.

warnings.text: Transference must never be applied before the signs of death are complete: to transfer untimely is like killing the deities.

notes: RESTRICTED: no method recorded. Also one of the Six Yogas (other units).

name: Purification rite for the dead (byang chog)
method_summary: A rite with the peaceful and wrathful deities using the deceased's name card, to purify obscurations, guide the consciousness and burn the card as a sign of release.

name: Rites to avert death ('chi bslu)
method_summary: When signs of untimely death appear, ransom rites, saving animals' lives, long-life practices and effigies are used to avert it.

name: A-tri meditation
method_summary: Fixing the mind on a white letter A in a sphere of light, then dissolving the support and resting in the natural state, and integrating it with activity, in graded sessions.

name: Guru yoga of Tapihritsa
method_summary: Visualizing Tapihritsa, naked and crystal-clear, as the embodiment of the lineage, supplicating and uniting one's mind with his.

name: The Matri mantra (oṃ ma tri mu ye sa le 'du)
method_summary: Recitation of Bön's most common mantra, the heart mantra of the Mother of wisdom, for purification of the six realms.

name: Bön preliminaries
method_summary: Preliminaries of the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü and other cycles: impermanence, refuge, bodhicitta, purification, maṇḍala, guru yoga, each accumulated.
